tasks.title: Trade results in units of risk
tasks.request: Give the agents honest numbers about their closed trades, measured from the broker, to learn from: the result of each trade in units of the risk it started with, and statistics by kind of setup, instrument, session and side
tasks.summary: When a trade closes, the agent now gets its entry and exit prices, its first stop and target, and its result in units of the risk it started with; when that can't be known (no stop, missing prices, no price move) it is left empty with the reason, never guessed. The agent's results now show wins out of how many trades and the average result in risk units, grouped the way it asks, over the period it chooses, and for the whole team when it asks. Lonora sees each agent's results and the owner's own trades separately. The weekly report facts carry the same numbers.

items.note: New: works out each closed trade's prices, starting stop and result in risk units from the broker's records and the order journal, and only reads them.
The message an agent gets when its trade closes carries those facts; it still never repeats text the agent wrote on its orders.
Results show wins out of how many, money and risk units per group, for one agent or the team.
The results question can now ask for a grouping, a start date and the team.
The agent's results tool explains the new numbers and choices.
The account summary an agent reads when it wakes explains the new numbers as facts to weigh, not rules.
The weekly report facts add the agent's results for the week and since it started.
New: checks the risk-unit results for stops on the order or set later, no stop, partial exits, adds, costs and a reversal.
Checks the groupings and what Lonora and a team agent each see of the team.

tasks.title: Lonora Cloud server: safety fixes
tasks.request: Check the findings of a review of the one-server rework and fix the real ones with small changes
tasks.summary: Activating an account can no longer wipe a customer that was set up by hand under the same name; staff are asked to pick another name. Building a new version no longer blocks activations, a version that fails for one customer still moves the others and names the ones left behind, a damaged customer disk no longer stops the whole server from starting, and live chat updates are passed on at once as on the current server.

items.note: Refuses a name already in use without removing anything, waits at most a minute for another job, builds a version without holding up activations, reports customers it could not move, and marks each customer disk as optional at start-up.
When the installer changed nothing, the attempt is not undone, so another customer's installation is never removed.
Passes each customer's live chat updates on at once, as the current server does.
Checks that activating an account never removes an installation made by hand under the same name.

tasks.title: Lonora Cloud on one server
tasks.request: Rework the website and activation for one Hostinger server that holds the website, the admin panel and every customer (D48), with the least code
tasks.summary: The website now runs on the shared server itself instead of Cloudflare, with the same handlers. Activate creates the customer's own Lonora there in under a minute, and each new version is built once and every customer moved to it. Removed: the Cloudflare settings file, the Hetzner and Cloudflare provisioning and the server's ready callback. Tested in practice mode only; not yet run on the real server.

items.note: New on the map: the website, the admin panel and the shared server's tools for customers.
New: creates, updates and removes one customer's Lonora with its own database, keys and address, and builds each version once for all customers.
New: serves the website and admin panel on the server and runs the existing handlers unchanged in shape.
Activate now asks the shared server for the customer's Lonora instead of renting a Hetzner server and a Cloudflare address.
Staff are recognised from the server's own sign-in instead of Cloudflare Access.
One click now ends with an active account; deleting removes the customer's installation.
Tests activation, failure and retry, deletion and a release with the real installer in practice mode.
New: checks the website server over real web requests.

tasks.title: Open Lonora from a link
tasks.request: Activating a customer's account is one click, and the customer opens their Lonora from the website
tasks.summary: A new customer's setup link now opens the first-run step with its one-time code already filled in, on the web and in the phone app. The phone app asks before it switches to the server the link names.

items.note: New: takes the one-time setup code from the link the website gives a customer, once, so they don't have to copy it by hand.
The first-run screen opens straight on the owner-setup step with the code filled in when the customer came from a setup link.
New: the screen a Lonora link opens in the phone app; it shows which server the link points to and connects only after the customer confirms.
New: refuses unsafe server addresses in a link and keeps the setup code only in memory, with the server it came for, until sign-in uses it.

Fills the setup code from the link into the owner-setup form, once and only for the linked server. It reads a newly confirmed link each time it comes into view, so a link confirmed while sign-in is open fills that form too.
Wipes a setup link's one-time code from the address bar when the app starts, so it never stays there when the first-run step does not open.
New: browser checks that a setup link's code leaves the address bar on an installation that already has its owner, and while the owner is signed in.
Adds checks that a confirmed Lonora link fills the setup code, from a fresh start and while sign-in is already open.

tasks.title: Agent prompts: properties not replies, one language fact, delegated requests (PA1-PA3)
tasks.request: Internal prompts in English only, no development examples or quoted replies in what the model reads, the reply language as one fact, and model-written requests never treated as the owner's words.
tasks.summary: Bundled prompts and skills lost their worked examples, quoted replies and retired authority words, and the loader now refuses them. The owner's reply language is any language tag; the server's own text follows the conversation's language instead of guessing from Arabic letters. A routine's, Task's or helper's prompt is a delegated request, and model-written decision summaries and non-bundled skill descriptions moved out of the system role.

items.change: Refuses bundled text with an Example line or a quoted first-person reply.
items.note: The skills and prompts were rewritten as lists of properties.

items.change: Decides Arabic or English for server text from any reply-language tag.
items.note: Read once per run in the run executor.

items.change: Widens the reply language to a language tag.
The old Arabic-letter guess is gone; a delegated request is a request, not the owner's message.
Delegated prompts are labelled; decision summaries are context data.
Trust labels are one fixed list, checked when a section is made.
A restored or steered run reads skill hints from its own delegated request, not an older owner message.

tasks.title: Agent prompts: the door's verdict, effect stages, a clock and dated history (PA4, PA5, PA7, PA8)
tasks.request: The agent never claims an action happened without a record, is told what the server actually does with a trade, knows the time, and sees when earlier messages were written.
tasks.summary: The permission note now gives the mode, pause and one sentence per kind of trade request, computed beside the execution door from what the door reads, so a Full agent on a voice call is no longer told to wait for approval. Alerts, workspace commands, action cards and agent creation report what actually happened, and a failed or uncertain action is carried into later runs. Every request ends with the clock in UTC and the owner's time zone, and replayed owner, card and peer turns carry their date and origin.

items.change: New: what the door does with new risk, risk reduction and another's ticket.
items.note: The door's own code is unchanged; one test compares the two.

items.change: Renders mode, pause, observe-only and the verdict sentences; the grant data and repeated rules are gone.
The voice call's instructions use the same new-risk verdict sentence.
An alert's effect and note follow whether it showed, waits or was kept back.
Keeps failed and uncertain actions from earlier runs.
items.note: Uncertain ones are marked to check before any repeat.

items.change: The clock that ends every request; the routing note no longer carries a changing read time.
Replayed owner, card and peer turns end with their date and origin.
items.note: The agent's own turns carry none.
